description: Turning a markdown-ish reply into the text that is spoken (spec #100 slice 2.5, ticket #160). Fenced code (``` to the next ```, non-greedy, across lines; an unclosed fence is no fence) becomes U+FFFC before the language is decided, once, on that text (language.json); then every U+FFFC Character becomes the code-omitted phrase, "code omitted", or "（代码已省略）" when the decision is zh, spliced in with no spaces added. Then, in this fixed order and with NSRegularExpression (ICU) semantics: inline code `x` keeps x (it may cross lines); [text](url) and ![alt](url) keep the text (the url ends at the first ), the text at the first ]); line-start heading markers ^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+ and quote markers ^\s{0,3}>\s? go (a line starts after any Unicode line terminator, and \s is White_Space, line breaks included, so these can swallow blank lines); **x**, *x*, __x__, _x_ and ~~x~~ keep x, in that order and across lines; line-start bullets ^\s{0,3}[-*+]\s+ go (after emphasis, so star bullets can pair as italic markers first); every remaining # * _ > and backtick goes; every run of White_Space becomes one space and the result is trimmed of .whitespacesAndNewlines (which, unlike the collapse, includes U+200B). When maxChars > 0 and the result is longer than maxChars Characters (extended grapheme clusters, never scalars or UTF-16 units), the first maxChars Characters are kept up to and including the last sentence ender among . ! ? 。 ！ ？ … (each compared as a whole Character, so one a combining mark extends is no ender), or all of them when the window holds none, trimmed; then " … reply truncated." follows after a space, or "……回复已截断。" with no space when the decision is zh. maxChars of 0 or less never truncates. Every case's input is in English or has no language, so only the English phrases appear; spoken-reply.json pins the language.
function: TTSService.speechText(fromMarkdown:maxChars:) — input {text, maxChars} with text a text descriptor (a string, or a list of strings and {repeat, times} parts joined in order), expected the spoken string (a text descriptor)
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md TTSService contract, v1.1 D, v1.2 A, v2.14; Tests/PowerUpTests/SpeechFixtureTests.swift testSpeechTextTable plays it through TTSService.speechText(fromMarkdown:maxChars:). Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/speech.rs speech_text_cases runs speech::speech_text, and speech_text_is_the_spoken_reply_text checks it is speech::spoken_reply's text.
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 Foundation and NaturalLanguage (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 67659a4

cases.name: a fenced code block collapses

input.text:
Here is the fix:
```swift
let x = 1
```
All done.

cases.expected: Here is the fix: code omitted All done.
cases.reason: A fence becomes the code-omitted phrase between the prose around it, never read out (HK-214, HK-215; SpeechTextTests.testFencedCodeBlocksCollapse).

cases.name: inline markdown is stripped
cases.expected: Use swift build to compile the project now.
cases.reason: Inline code, bold, a link and underscore emphasis lose their syntax and keep their text (HK-215; SpeechTextTests.testInlineMarkdownIsStripped).

> quoted line

* second item
plain

cases.expected: Title quoted line first item second item plain
cases.reason: Line-start heading, quote and bullet markers are dropped (HK-215; SpeechTextTests.testHeadingsQuotesAndBulletsAreStripped).

cases.name: whitespace collapses
cases.reason: Any run of whitespace is one space (HK-215; SpeechTextTests.testWhitespaceCollapses).

cases.name: zero maxChars means no limit
cases.reason: A limit of 0 never truncates, however long the reply (HK-216; SpeechTextTests.testZeroMaxCharsMeansNoLimit).

cases.name: truncation cuts at a sentence boundary

cases.reason: The cut falls after the last sentence ender in the window and the English suffix follows a space (HK-216; SpeechTextTests.testTruncationCutsAtSentenceBoundary).

cases.name: no sentence boundary hard cuts
cases.reason: Without an ender in the window the window itself is kept (HK-216; SpeechTextTests.testTruncationWithoutSentenceBoundaryHardCuts).

cases.name: short text is untouched
cases.reason: Text within the limit gets no suffix (HK-216; SpeechTextTests.testShortTextIsUntouched).

cases.name: two fences become two phrases

cases.reason: The fence match is non-greedy, so the prose between two fences is kept (HK-214).

cases.reason: The phrase replaces the fence exactly, with no space added around it (HK-214).

cases.name: an unterminated fence is left to the later rules
cases.reason: Only a closed fence is a fence; an open one is stripped as stray backticks (HK-214).

cases.name: a fence spans blank lines
cases.reason: The fence pattern crosses any line breaks, blank lines included (HK-214).

cases.name: a literal object replacement character reads as code omitted
cases.reason: Every U+FFFC is replaced by the phrase, the reply's own included, because the placeholder is that character (HK-214).

cases.name: an object replacement character a combining mark extends is kept
cases.reason: The placeholder swap compares Characters, so U+FFFC with a combining acute is a different Character and survives (HK-214).

cases.name: inline code keeps its content
cases.reason: Each backtick pair goes and its content stays (HK-215).

cases.name: inline code spans a line break

cases.name: an unpaired backtick is dropped
